Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Breathing difficulty and rash after a wasp sting ~15 minutes prior while gardening.
- Symptoms: Shallow breathing and chest tightness; tingling sensation in lips; blotchy rash on body. Denies throat closing. Wheeze not reported. Lip swelling not confirmed (uncertain).
- Prior similar episodes: None.
- Treatments taken prior to call: None.
- Past medical history: Eczema; aerosinusitis. No other significant PMH reported. Past surgeries not discussed.
- Medications: No regular medications documented. Has antihistamines at home used for flying (dose/route/frequency not documented); not taken yet at time of call.
- Social history: Wife present and able to assist; other details not documented.
- Allergies: Penicillin (reaction details not documented).

Objective:
- Telehealth consult; no physical examination or vital signs documented.
- No investigations performed or available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute allergic reaction to wasp sting; risk of anaphylaxis
   - Assessment or likely diagnosis: Acute allergic reaction to wasp sting; risk of anaphylaxis.
   - Differential diagnosis: Uncomplicated urticarial reaction vs evolving anaphylaxis.
   - Treatment planned: Immediate activation of emergency services (wife instructed to call ambulance); take an oral antihistamine now while awaiting EMS (specific drug/dose/route/frequency not documented); urgent transport to hospital for evaluation and management.
   - Relevant referrals: Emergency Department via ambulance.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vital signs (HR, BP, RR, SpO2, temp), focused airway/resp exam (voice changes, stridor, wheeze), extent and distribution of rash/angioedema, GI symptoms, exact site of sting and whether stinger removed, history of asthma or prior venom reactions, current medication list and doses, detailed penicillin allergy reaction, confirmation of lip swelling, epinephrine autoinjector availability/use, smoking/alcohol history.
- Internal conflicts: Lip swelling not confirmed (patient reported lip tingling; did not directly confirm or deny swelling).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; some incomplete responses and brief pauses; no objective measurements available.
